title: The Depths — Xan-Kor's Chamber
subject: A vast underground chamber containing an enormous dormant war-engine — not a creature, not a god, but a biomechanical construct built for ritual devastation with surgical precision. The construct is imprisoned between realities and barely present in ours: something colossal is down there, but it is almost impossible to make out — the eye catches only scattered fragments and cannot assemble them into a whole. The viewer is looking down into the chamber from above, straining to perceive something that should not exist and is mostly not here.
setting: The deepest level beneath the Nodrum facility. The chamber is far larger than anything above it suggested — the entire facility was built on top of this. The architecture here is older than everything else, predating civilization as the world understands it.

architecture.chamber: A cylindrical or polygonal shaft descending deep into the earth. The walls are smooth-cut stone with precise geometric channels carved into them, all converging downward toward the central form. No decoration, no artistry — pure function. This space was engineered, not designed.
architecture.energy_lines: Lines of amber light run down the wall channels and into the containment frames around the construct. They trace the architecture and the clamps — they do NOT pool, halo, or converge into a bright glowing core, sphere, or ring at the center. Some lines are bright and active, others dim or dormant, suggesting partial activation.
architecture.central_form: Xan-Kor itself, at the bottom of the shaft. Enormous, biomechanical, dormant — but almost entirely phase-shifted OUT of this reality, so only the faintest trace of it is perceptible. This is NOT a blur, glow, mist, or shimmer around it, and there is NO bubble, sphere, dome, membrane, or aura enclosing it. The construct is spatially displaced and overwhelmingly absent: the vast majority of its mass is simply not here — transparent, vanished, or swallowed by the dark, the empty chamber visible straight through where colossal metal should be. Render it like a heavily misaligned multiple exposure broken almost to nothing — a few faint, offset, semi-transparent echoes of bronze structure that do not register with one another, with subtle red/cyan chromatic separation along the displaced contours. Only two or three SMALL fragments anywhere on it resolve into sharp, solid, crisply detailed metal — just enough to prove the dislocation is real and selective rather than softness laid over the picture; everything else is fugitive, incomplete, and refuses to cohere into a recognisable form. The viewer should sense immense scale and menace while being unable to actually trace its shape. The boundary between 'here' and 'not here' runs jaggedly and irregularly through the construct's own body — never a smooth circle, ring, or enclosing zone. The slivers that do resolve hint at something between a siege engine and an anatomy — precision-machined bronze shaped with organic curves, joints, and segments — but the whole stays unreadable. It is curled or folded inward, compact, waiting. Not sleeping — *stored*.
architecture.containment: Bronze clamps, geometric barrier-frames, and alignment locks surround the construct. These are the containment systems — some intact, some loosened or adjusted by the Triune's work.

mood: Awe and existential dread. The feeling of standing at the edge of a missile silo and realizing what the warhead is for. This is not evil — it is purpose without conscience. The scale makes everything above feel fragile.
lighting: Amber energy lines provide the primary light, tracing the walls and containment frames — not pooling into a central glow. The construct is not haloed or backlit: its solid portions catch dim amber off the channels while its displaced portions are simply dark, transparent, or absent. The upper edges of the chamber where the viewer stands are dim. Deep shadow fills the lowest reaches.
color_palette: amber energy lines — brighter here than anywhere else in the facility
tarnished bronze of the construct's visible surfaces
cold gray stone of the chamber walls
faint pale light reflecting off machined metal surfaces
no green, no warmth, no organic color
composition: Looking down from a high vantage point — the edge of a balcony, a broken walkway, or an opening in the floor of the level above. Vertigo-inducing depth. The eye is drawn down the shaft toward where the construct should be, but it almost isn't there — only a scatter of faint displaced fragments hangs in the dark, the immense scale implied by the architecture and the void rather than by any visible body. The viewer feels small and unsure of what they are even looking at.
details: CRITICAL: the chamber walls, geometric channels, energy lines, containment frames, and the viewer's vantage point are all rendered crisp, tack-sharp, and fully solid. The construct is the ONLY thing affected — and it is affected by extreme spatial DISPLACEMENT (mostly absent/transparent, a few faint offset ghost-echoes, only tiny solid fragments), NOT by blur, haze, soft focus, or a surrounding energy effect. The sharp, solid surroundings make unmistakably clear this is the object being phase-shifted almost entirely out of reality, not a focus or image-quality problem

Only a few small fragments of the construct are precision biomechanical bronze, sharp and detailed; the overwhelming majority is absent — the empty dark chamber visible straight through, as though nearly all of that metal is currently somewhere else
Some containment clamps are visibly loosened or repositioned — evidence of the Triune's tampering
A few energy lines pulse brighter than others, suggesting partial systems coming online
The walls show no inscriptions or decoration — only functional geometry, channels, and mounting points
style: Painterly fantasy illustration with a strong sense of scale and atmosphere. The tone of looking into the heart of something ancient and terrible — akin to discovering a buried weapon from a forgotten war between forces beyond mortal understanding. Dark concept art, heavy on shadow and implied form rather than full reveal.
aspect_ratio: 9:16 portrait or 2:3 portrait — vertical composition to emphasize the depth of the shaft
do_not_include: characters or figures for scale — the architecture itself communicates scale
the full solid form of Xan-Kor clearly resolved — it must read as displaced, offset, and barely in this reality, with the overwhelming majority missing or transparent
a legible, readable, traceable, or recognisable construct silhouette — the viewer must NOT be able to make out its overall shape; only scattered fragments survive
force field, energy shield, bubble, dome, glowing sphere or orb, aura, halo, portal ring, or any containment energy field around the construct

any smooth circular or spherical boundary, membrane, glowing zone, fog, mist, or haze cloud enclosing or surrounding the construct — the phasing is ragged and lives in the body itself, with no enclosing shape
blur, soft focus, or low quality applied to the whole image — the surrounding architecture must be sharp and solid; the construct is displaced, not blurred
any visual that reads as a camera/lens defect rather than a deliberate in-world phase-displacement of the construct
glowing eyes or any suggestion of consciousness or awareness
organic corruption, flesh, or body horror — this is mechanical, not biological
lava, fire, or hellish imagery — this is cold precision, not infernal
any suggestion this is a dragon, golem, or conventional fantasy creature
